verdicts.evidence: pattern-mapper.md:19 — "Dispatched by the orchestrator/pipeline (between research and planning steps)." (verified verbatim; also frontmatter line 3 "dispatched by the orchestrator/pipeline before planning")
verdicts.reasoning: KICKOFF.md line 390 (queue says 389 — the whole queue's line ranges are off by one; the quoted text is verbatim at 390) reads "Now that PHASE/CONTEXT.md and PHASE/RESEARCH.md both exist, dispatch the pattern-mapper agent". The agent states its pipeline position in the abstract but has no means to observe or enforce dispatch timing — it cannot know that the two preceding blocks of the SAME step have already produced their outputs. Ordering/serialization across skills is load-bearing by the audit's own rule. The systemic flag also checks out: KICKOFF.md lines 369-371 carry the same rationale ("pattern-mapper is deliberately NOT in this fan-out: it reads PHASE/CONTEXT.md and PHASE/RESEARCH.md, neither of which exists yet, so it gets its own block below"), so the two locations are genuinely the same constraint stated twice inside the guide — an intra-guide redundancy, not a skill duplication. KEEP.

verdicts.evidence: pattern-mapper.md:25 — "- Extract list of files to be created or modified from CONTEXT.md and RESEARCH.md"; :27 "- Search the codebase for the closest existing analog per file"; :28 "- Read each analog and extract concrete code excerpts (imports, auth patterns, core pattern, error handling)"; :29 "- Produce PATTERNS.md with per-file pattern assignments and code to copy from" (all verified verbatim)
verdicts.reasoning: KICKOFF.md lines 391-393 ("it extracts the list of files this phase will create or modify from those two documents and writes PHASE/PATTERNS.md, mapping each file to its closest existing analog with concrete code excerpts to copy") maps clause-for-clause onto the four <role> core-responsibility bullets at lines 25/27/28/29, and again onto the frontmatter description at line 3 ("Analyzes codebase for existing patterns and produces PATTERNS.md mapping new files to closest analogs"). I looked for a residue the agent cannot know and found none: the two input document names are already at line 25, "closest existing analog" is line 27's exact phrasing, "concrete code excerpts" is line 28's exact phrasing, and the output-path fragment is carved out into claim pattern-mapper-3. Nothing here selects a mode, gates a condition, or substitutes a value. Confirmed duplication; medium because it is the entire descriptive middle of the block, not a stray phrase.

Output path / directory convention, which the audit rules class as an invocation argument. Verified non-drifting on both sides: the agent's line 14 note says `PHASE_DIR` is orchestrator-supplied per invocation, so the operator does have to supply the directory half, and the sitemap agrees — references/doc-sitemap.md:81 lists `PATTERNS.md` under `phases/<NN>-<slug>/`, and :159 defines `PHASE/` = `docs/milestones/<M>/phases/<NN>-<slug>/`. Weakest of the three load-bearing claims, because the filename itself (as opposed to the directory) is hardcoded by line 155 and is therefore known to the agent; but the surviving value is real — step 7 at KICKOFF.md:486 refers to `PHASE/PATTERNS.md` by name, so the artifact name has to be established here. KEEP, low.

verdicts.evidence: pattern-mapper.md:82 — "Orchestrator provides: phase number/name, phase directory, CONTEXT.md path, RESEARCH.md path." (verified verbatim, <execution_flow> Step 1)
verdicts.reasoning: KICKOFF.md lines 393-394 enumerate exactly the four items line 82 declares it expects to receive. This is the caller side of a two-sided contract: line 82 is the receiver's declaration that it will NOT discover these itself, so something has to actually pass them, and only the operator prompt can. The enumeration is a near-verbatim mirror and could be compressed to "give it the standard scope inputs", so there is a compression opportunity — but deleting it would leave the agent's stated inputs unsupplied. KEEP, low.

verdicts.evidence: pattern-mapper.md:49 — "**CONTEXT.md** (if exists) — User decisions captured during phase discussion"; :57 — "**RESEARCH.md** (if exists) — Technical research from phase-researcher" (both verified verbatim)
verdicts.reasoning: I re-ran the absence hunt myself rather than trusting the claim. Grepping pattern-mapper.md for `if exists|missing|absent|abort|halt|refuse|do not invent|fabricat|empty|not exist|unavailable|precondition|prerequisite` returns ONLY lines 49 and 57 — there is no guard anywhere. <success_criteria> (lines 320-328) requires "All files from CONTEXT.md and RESEARCH.md classified" but never requires that list to be non-empty; the only stopping rules in <critical_rules> (lines 310-314) are about re-reads, large files, and stopping at 3-5 analogs. The "No Analog Found" section (line 261) covers a missing ANALOG, not a missing upstream document. So the gap is real: dispatched early, the agent treats both inputs as optional, falls through to "Implied files — files inferred from features described" (line 86), and produces a fabricated file list rather than refusing. The KICKOFF warning is compensating and must be KEPT. Severity lowered from medium to low: the ordering it protects is already stated twice in KICKOFF (lines 369-371 and 390), the residual blast radius is a wrong file list rather than fabricated code (analogs are still read from real source), and the operator can never delegate dispatch timing to the agent anyway — the skill-side fix (fail loudly when both upstream docs are absent or yield no files) is a hardening, not a replacement for this sentence.

verdicts.evidence: pattern-mapper.md:67 — "Your PATTERNS.md is consumed by `planner`:" followed by a three-row table (lines 69-73) describing how planner uses `## File Classification`, `## Pattern Assignments`, and `## Shared Patterns`
verdicts.reasoning: Verified the absence independently rather than accepting the claim's grep. `grep -rn "PATTERNS.md"` across all of plugins/ returns four files: doc-sitemap.md (x2, path listing only), pattern-mapper.md itself, and skills/plan-review-goal-backward/SKILL.md (lines 44 and 106) — planner.md is NOT among them. Grepping agents/planner.md and its whole references/planning/ chain for `pattern-mapper|PATTERNS.md|analog` yields exactly one hit, planner.md:1215 ("There is no benefit to reading more analogs of the same pattern"), an unrelated stop-reading rule. planner.md's own input-loading block (lines 975-985) cats CONTEXT.md, RESEARCH.md and DISCOVERY.md and has has_context/has_research conditionals — PATTERNS.md is conspicuously absent from that list. So pattern-mapper's <downstream_consumer> table asserts a handoff that neither end implements, and the only thing that actually delivers PATTERNS.md to the planner is the guide: this sentence plus its payoff at KICKOFF.md:486 ("Read PHASE/PATTERNS.md and cite its per-file..."). LOAD-BEARING, must be KEPT; high severity because without it pattern-mapper's sole output is orphaned from its declared consumer, and the real defect is planner.md's missing input plus pattern-mapper's aspirational table.
